first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior onboarding and signup simplification experiments showed durable activation and time-to-value gains. I would verify those records, while also checking the promotional-pricing evidence because competitor pricing creates a plausible alternative. Run a guarded onboarding simplification test with downstream qualified-revenue and lead-quality monitoring rather than immediately discounting.

final.rationale: Use this week’s slot on a standard, segment-aware onboarding simplification experiment. Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%, while the verified onboarding record shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention. Signup simplification also improved SMB activation, but its slight retention decline and segment-specific result argue for monitoring downstream retention and qualified revenue. Do not pursue the 40% discount: despite +18% qualified revenue initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive renewal.
